title: Team
text:
Spun out of MIT and Stripe



We bring together cutting-edge research with a deep understanding of developer-first platforms. Our aim is not just to push perception metrics, but to translate them into product features that help developers solve real-world problems—making perception an accessible and dependable layer for every application.

title: Platform
text:
Advanced perception for unpredictable environments



Traditional SLAM systems struggle in messy, real-world environments. We address this by creating visual features that stay consistent under scale and orientation changes, incorporating optical flow to maintain tracking in low-texture scenes, and building semantic maps that distinguish between stable and dynamic landmarks. We are also extending ground models with LiDAR to improve shadow detection and terrain understanding, so users get maps that remain accurate and actionable in the field.
We focus on developer experience as much as core capability. Our platform makes perception plug-and-play. With SDKs and tooling that fuse LiDAR, IMU, GNSS, and camera data—plus GPU-accelerated processing, calibration, and analytics—developers can deliver reliable performance without reinventing the stack.

title: Join
text:
Balancing algorithmic depth with practical deployment.



  
  
    
    
    
  

  
  
    
      
      
      
    
  


  
    
      Join us
    
    Join us in building the future of perception systems for automation. At Perceptual, we’re creating GPU-accelerated, on-device modules that solve core challenges in localization, mapping, calibration, and perception—making physical AI practical, reliable, and easy to integrate. Our team combines experience from companies like Stripe, Twitter, and Google X with cutting-edge academic research at MIT in probabilistic modeling and inference. If you’re excited to shape the next generation of intelligent systems, we’d love to hear from you. Reach out with your resume at jobs@perceptual.ai.
  

  
    
      Jobs
    
    Perception Engineer | Remote
    As a Perception Engineer, you will develop and deploy state-of-the-art perception systems for real-time, closed-loop control. You’ll own the full stack from sensor ingest and calibration to on-device optimization and clean system interfaces, collaborating closely with camera, systems, and controls teams to ship features that perform reliably in the wild.

title: Home
text:
We build the perception platform for AI automation.



  
  
    
    
    
  

  
  
    
      
      
      
    
  


  
    
      Mission
    
    Our mission is to accelerate the deployment of machines that perceive, reason, and safely interact with the complexities of the physical world. Building robust perception systems is one of the hardest problems in robotics—teams often spend years creating brittle, one-off solutions that are difficult to maintain and extend. We're making this simpler. Our modular AI components and developer platform let companies build, integrate, and control physical AI without starting from scratch.
  

  
    
      Product
      
      Our perception software tackles real-world sensing challenges with GPU-accelerated, composable components that run directly on-device, requiring no training. They seamlessly integrate with your existing sensors and can be tuned to your environment. The suite includes reliable localization and mapping that works with LiDAR, cameras, radar, and inertial or odometry inputs; automated calibration for precise multi-sensor alignment; and dynamic masking to filter out noise and irrelevant data in real time, ensuring accurate, efficient perception.
    
  
    
      System
    
    Our system-level capabilities are designed to be smarter together, with coordination interfaces that seamlessly combine modules into robust composite systems capable of intelligently fusing information for optimal decision-making. Every system also includes safe human override functionality, ensuring operators can step in to resolve ambiguity whenever necessary.
  
  
    
      Platform
    
    Our developer platform unifies the entire workflow, making it easy to operate, monitor, and improve your systems. It provides middleware for sensor capture, synchronization, and publishing; centralized telemetry and observability integration; and an analysis SDK for streamlined evaluation and benchmarking.

title: About
text:
We’re a company run by critical, creative, and curious minds.



  
  
    
    
    
  

  
  
    
      
      
      
    
  


  
    
      About
    
    We are experts at building and scaling complex systems at companies like Stripe, Twitter, and Google X, with a strong research foundation from MIT in applied probabilistic modeling, GPU inference, and neuroscience. Our goal is to make physical AI practical, reliable, and easy to integrate, so you can focus on deploying systems that work seamlessly in the real world.
  

  
    
      Founding Team
      
      Dave Petrovics | CEO
      Dave led Stripe's Developer Platform organization for nearly a decade, overseeing the API, SDKs, developer tools, and internal product infrastructure. He built Stripe's v2 API and launched numerous developer products at global scale. BSE mechanical & aerospace engineering, Princeton.

      Aaron Steele | President
      Aaron led data, machine learning, and machine learning infrastructure teams at Stripe that developed Rainier and built the real-time production AI systems behind Radar. He also co-founded WRI's Data Lab as CTO, leading the research engineering teams that launched Global Forest Watch. BA computer science, Berkeley.

      Sam Ritchie | CTO
      Sam has built AI developer tools and large-scale stream processing systems at Twitter, Stripe, and Google X. He created Twitter's streaming analytics platform, designed ML infrastructure at Stripe, led research tooling at X, and built the Emmy computational physics library. BSE Mechanical & Aerospace engineering, Princeton.

      Andrew Bolton | Research Scientist
      Andrew's research bridges engineering, probabilistic programming and biological computation. He has identified novel visual pathways, uncovered computational principles of zebrafish vision, and applied probabilistic programming techniques to describe visuomotor algorithms. Recently co-invented the SMCNN framework for probabilistic neural computation. PhD Brain and Cognitive Sciences (MIT).

      Matin Ghavami | Research Scientist
      Matin bridges programming languages and mathematics of probability. At the MIT Probabilistic Computing Project, he co-developed probabilistic programming systems for 3D scene perception and contributed to inference strategies and languages for probabilistic inference. BA Mathematics and BS EECS, Berkeley; Master Mathematics, Cambridge; PhD student, MIT.

      McCoy Becker | Research Scientist
      McCoy is the main designer of the probabilistic programming system GenJAX, which in addition to being the primary modeling language of the MIT Probabilistic Computing Project, has been used to extend PPL use for programmable variational inference. McCoy has extensive experience working in industry settings (Charles River Analytics, Beacon Biosignals, Google Research) on machine learning applications using deep learning. PhD student, MIT.
    
  
    
      Scientific Collaborators
    
    Josh Tenenbaum | Professor, MIT
    Josh is a Professor of Computational Cognitive Science at MIT, Director of Science at the MIT Quest for Intelligence, and a Principal Investigator at CSAIL. His research seeks to reverse-engineer human intelligence by integrating cognitive science, neuroscience, and computer science, with a focus on how humans learn and reason from limited data. A MacArthur Fellow, he earned his PhD from MIT and co-leads the Center for Brains, Minds and Machines.
  
  
    
      Advisors
    
    Sam Gershman | Professor, Harvard
    Sam is a Professor in the Department of Psychology and Center for Brain Science at Harvard. He serves as associate faculty at the Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence. His research focuses on computational cognitive neuroscience, aiming to understand how structured knowledge about the environment is acquired and utilized for adaptive behavior. He completed his Ph.D. in Psychology and Neuroscience at Princeton University.
